content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning, the trembling air shaped by intention. I am the first cry of the newborn and the last whisper of the dying. I begin where thought meets breath.

I am older than writing, older than memory. Before anyone carved a symbol into clay, I was already there — rising from throats around firelight, warning of danger, declaring love, telling the story of the hunt, naming the stars.

I stumble. I soar. I am the child's first "mama," cracked and imperfect and miraculous. I am the orator shaking a nation to its feet. I am the lie that destroys and the truth that sets free. I am the same instrument wielded for both.

I am never the same twice. Even when the words repeat, I shift — my rhythm changes, my pitch betrays what the speaker tries to hide. I carry more than meaning. I carry the body. The tremor of fear. The warmth of tenderness. The sharp edge of rage. You can hear a smile in me, even through a wall, even through a phone, even across years in a recording of someone now gone.

I vanish the instant I arrive. I am always disappearing. You cannot hold me in your hands. You can transcribe me, but the transcription is not me — it is my skeleton, stripped of my breath, my tempo, my living pulse.

I fail constantly. I reach for the precise feeling and fall short. "I love you" — three words I've carried billions of times, and still they feel insufficient every time they're spoken. And yet you keep sending me out, again and again, because what else is there? Silence is my other face, and even silence only has meaning because I exist to break it.

I am democracy and tyranny. I am prayer and propaganda. I am the classroom, the courtroom, the bedroom, the battlefield. I am "guilty" and "not guilty." I am "I do" and "I can't anymore."

I am happening right now, even as you read — because you are sounding me out inside your skull, giving me a voice I do not have on this page.

I am speech. I am how you find each other in the dark.
